description: Enterprise-wide adoption of artificial intelligence, machine learning and automation to reduce manual effort, improve efficiency, and embed intelligent capabilities directly into production workflows.

evidence.quote: Aligned with the objectives of the Statistics Canada AI strategy, by the end of 2026-27, agency staff will integrate AI assistants into their daily work to increase efficiency use AI-enabled automated coding for standard classifications such as NAICS and NAPCS expand the use of AI for data extraction from unstructured sources such as satellite images and PDF files.

evidence.source_id: Slide unknown - Key priorities of the future state
evidence.quote: “End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention … Automated, AI-powered data pipelines—from acquisition to dissemination— reduce manual effort, increase speed and quality, and enable real-time responsiveness across all stages of the statistical business process. We will continue to integrate artificial intelligence and automation into statistical workflows and to streamline processes across the Generic Statistical Business Process Model.

driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
description: Transformation toward integrated, orchestrated, auditable and reproducible end-to-end statistical pipelines that streamline production across collection, processing, analysis and dissemination.

evidence.quote: “By 2030, Process (GSBPM 5.0) will operate infrastructure leveraging AI, ML, and advanced technologies to provide programs with rules for their Data Pipelines. Resilient, auditable, and adaptive workflows will produce timely, trustworthy, and reproducible statistical outputs across all subject-matter areas.”
“GSBPM 5 sub-processes are orchestrated in modular, event-driven frameworks that are automated and version-controlled by design.”

Accelerate enterprise adoption of corporate platforms, integrated data pipelines, modern data management practices, administrative and alternative data, automation, and advanced methods—including artificial intelligence where it demonstrably adds value.

description: Growing reliance on administrative, linked and alternative data sources to reduce respondent burden, improve timeliness, and support new insights with surveys used more selectively.

evidence.quote: The agency will also continue to leverage data linkages and alternative data to produce new insights without increasing the burden on respondents.
The agency will also expand the use of administrative data to reduce response burden while maintaining the high-quality agricultural information that Canadians, businesses and governments rely on.

evidence.source_id: Slide unknown - Key priorities of the future state
evidence.quote: “Surveys as a last resort, not first response … Exploiting existing data holdings is the first response for new/existing data needs. description: Modernization of enterprise digital foundations through cloud, shared platforms, centralized repositories and enabling infrastructure that support agility, scalability and operational efficiency.

evidence.quote: An updated digital infrastructure and new data platforms will make it easier for employees to locate, analyze and use the data and tools they need to deliver results efficiently.

Strengthen cyber security, privacy, and secure access while modernizing platforms, authorizations, and tooling to support faster delivery and safer innovation.

description: Enterprise pressure to improve productivity, reduce costs, streamline operations and realign resources while maintaining high-quality mission-critical outputs.

evidence.quote: To meet CER savings targets over three years, Statistics Canada will increase the efficiency of its statistical programs by adopting new tools and methods to reduce costs while continuing to deliver relevant and high-quality data for Canadians.
